messages:
incident-bot: 🚨 INCIDENT: production inference p99 latency spike detected in us-east-1. SLO breach triggered (p99 > 1.2s for 5m). On-call: @maya-k. Alert INC-2026-0423-07.

maya-k: I'm on it. Seeing lots of streaming stalls and chunked responses that hang mid-stream. p95/p99 for text.generate up across several routes.

samir: I can take control-plane (auth/config) — seeing a pile of 429s in auth-rate-limiter from runtime clients. Starting to tail auth logs now.

jordan: I'll own the runtime side (serving). If config fetchs are blocking KV cache warmup that could cause tail spikes.

maya-k: traces show a big wait at fetchUserConfig -> auth check -> config-service. fetchUserConfig p95 ~ 700ms, p99 ~ 1.6s. Previously ~20-40ms. Streaming sessions backlog increasing.

samir: auth-service logs: burst of retries from a new rate limiter policy deployed ~1h ago (policy id rl-2026-04-b). Lots of 429 then clients backoff+retry -> amplifying traffic.

maya-k: @samir can we temporarily whitelist runtime service or bump internal limits? We need quick mitigation to stop cascading retries.

samir: Doing both. Applying temporary whitelist for client-id runtime-prod in auth config and increasing internal limit from 100 -> 500 QPS. Pushing change to auth config store now.

samir: (command) ```curl -s -XPOST https://auth-admin/_whitelist -d '{"client":"runtime-prod","ttl":600}'``` -> 200 OK. Rate limit updated.

deploy-bot: config-change accepted. auth-service rollout started (3 nodes) via canary.

jordan: On runtime side we can short-circuit remote config fetch for in-flight requests. Setting env REDWOOD_ENABLE_REMOTE_CONFIG=false on canary pool. Rolling restart 5 pods.

maya-k: Will that break any customer-specific overrides? Only risk is a small subset of customers with recent flag changes. CS, heads-up.

customer-success: Noted. We have 3 active tickets reporting degraded streaming. Escalating to affected accounts, ETA for workaround?

dena: Confirming I will keep an eye for residual p99s and take the handoff at +30m. If auth errors persist we should enable local-cached config: REDWOOD_FORCE_LOCAL_CONFIG=true.

jordan: Applying the runtime env now. (kubectl) ```kubectl set env deploy/runtime-pool-canary REDWOOD_ENABLE_REMOTE_CONFIG=false --namespace=prod``` Rolling pods 3/5 -> 5/5.

maya-k: Monitoring dashboards: p99 falling from 1.6s -> 420ms within 90s of whitelist + config disable. Streaming stall rate down ~75%.

samir: Auth 429s dropped to near zero after whitelist. Underlying rate-limiter policy rl-2026-04-b has a bug in token refill that mis-estimates concurrent spikes. We'll revert that policy after incident.

jordan: Observed one customer stream that still tripped at ~18s. Looking at logs shows an edge case with large context + repeat config fetch. Pinned to cached config fixes it.

customer-success: CS updated customers with workaround: temporary degraded config freshness, but stable responses. Customers accepted temporary change for now.

maya-k: Impact assessment: ~4% of production requests saw p99 breach; streaming stalls mostly for sessions >10s; major customers affected: 3 accounts (ticket IDs CS-1021, CS-1023, CS-1024). No data loss, just latency.

samir: Immediate action items: 1) keep runtime remote config disabled for 30m, 2) revert faulty rl-2026-04-b policy, 3) deploy fix for token refill logic in rate-limiter, 4) add client-level backoff to limit retry storms.

dena: I'll take on #1 and #4 during my shift. Samir can you revert policy and open PR for rate-limiter fix?

samir: Reverting policy now and creating PR. PR: https://git.redwood/repo/pulls/4523 - rate limiter unit tests included.

deploy-bot: auth-policy revert applied to prod (rl-2026-04-b -> rl-2026-03-stable).

maya-k: Next steps & handoff: keeping mitigations for 30m, monitor p95/p99, if stable after 30m we'll gradually re-enable REDWOOD_ENABLE_REMOTE_CONFIG and remove whitelist. Handoff to @dena in 30m. If p99 > 500ms reopen page.

dena: Acknowledged. Will follow up with post-incident notes and root cause write-up (likely rate-limiter bug + no circuit-breaker on config fetch).

maya-k: Thanks all. Adding summary to incident tracker and CS notes.

incident-bot: Incident mitigated -> SLO at risk cleared. Start incident postmortem? Use template /incidents/new and tag eng-runtime, eng-ml, eng-sre, and product.
